transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?
Since my husband’s heart attack, it’s like I’m not really here. When I walk into his hospital room, everything feels unreal, like I’m watching it happen to someone else.
Do these unreal or detached feelings happen mainly when you’re thinking about your husband’s heart attack, and do they come with strong sadness or worry about the situation?

No, it's not just when I'm thinking about it—it happens when I walk into his ICU room or even when I'm just sitting in my own living room. Instead of feeling sad or worried, it's more of a heavy, numb blankness, like my emotions have been completely switched off. It really feels like I'm just watching someone else's life play out like a movie.
When you feel unreal or like you are watching life like a movie, do you still know that these feelings are just a sensation and that the world is actually real?

Yes, deep down I know it’s just a strange sensation and that I haven't actually lost my mind or physically left my body. But even though I know the world around me is real, that feeling of floating behind myself and seeing everything as dim and movie-like is still incredibly strong and unsettling.
Have these feelings of being unreal or detached been happening repeatedly for at least several months, or did they start only after your husband’s heart attack?
No, this has never happened to me before in my life. It only started six days ago, right after my husband collapsed at the kitchen table.

Since these feelings started six days ago, have they been getting better, staying the same, or getting worse? Have they made it hard for you to function at work, at home, or while caring for your husband?

They have been constant and haven't gotten any better since it happened six days ago. It has made it very hard to function—I've stopped going to my quilting circle, skipped my own doctor appointments, and I can't even organize myself to pay bills or cook. I just feel completely stuck at his bedside, unable to manage my normal life.
Since your husband’s heart attack, have you had any flashbacks, nightmares, trouble sleeping, being on edge, or trying to avoid reminders of what happened?

Yes, I keep seeing his face turn blue and hearing that awful gurgling sound out of nowhere, so I try not to think about that afternoon and even take the long way around the hospital to avoid the ER doors. I’m also incredibly jumpy and on edge—every little noise, like a monitor beeping or someone dropping a tray, makes me jump out of my skin and sends my heart racing.
Have these symptoms been present for less than a month, or have they continued for more than a month?
Oh, it has been much less than a month—it only started six days ago when my husband collapsed. It feels like an eternity, but it has really only been about six days since all of this began.
Have these symptoms continued for more than one month, or are they still within the first month after the stressful event?
They are still well within the first month. It has only been about six days since my husband collapsed and was rushed to the hospital.
Since your husband’s heart attack, have you had any nightmares, flashbacks, or unwanted memories that feel like you are reliving the event?

Yes, I keep having these terrible, unwanted memories pop into my mind out of nowhere, even when I'm just washing dishes or trying to read. I suddenly see his face turning that awful blue and hear that gurgling sound all over again. It feels like I'm right back at the kitchen table, with my hands slipping on his chest as I try to do CPR.
Did you directly experience, witness, or learn about a life-threatening or sexual trauma, or was the event mainly your husband’s medical emergency?

I directly witnessed the whole thing right in front of me at our kitchen table. He suddenly collapsed and turned blue, and I had to desperately try to perform CPR on him myself until the paramedics got there. Even though it was his medical emergency, I was right there experiencing the absolute terror of trying to save his life with my own hands.
Since this happened, do you also have nightmares, flashbacks, or strong avoidance of reminders of the event, like places or thoughts connected to it?

I don't really have nightmares, but I definitely get vivid flashbacks during the day where I see his blue face and feel like I'm right back there doing CPR. Because of that, I actively avoid thinking about that afternoon and even take the long way around the hospital to avoid the ER doors and ambulances, since seeing them makes me feel like I might fall apart.
Have your symptoms been improving at all since the event, or are they still severe and causing major problems with daily functioning?

No, they haven't gotten any better at all over these past six days. They are still very severe and have completely disrupted my life—I've stopped going to my quilting circle, skipped my own doctor appointments, and can't even manage basic tasks like paying bills or cooking a proper meal.
Since the event, have you had any moments of feeling numb, detached from your emotions, or like the world is unreal or dreamlike?

Yes, absolutely. It feels like I'm floating a few feet behind myself watching some other old woman visit her husband, with everything looking dim and far away like a movie. I also feel completely numb and "switched off" inside, carrying this heavy blankness where I can't even feel happy or warm when my friends from the quilting circle bring me good news.

Before your husband’s collapse, had you ever had a traumatic event like this that led to flashbacks, avoidance, or feeling constantly on edge, or is this the first time these symptoms have ever happened?
No, I’ve never experienced anything like this before in my entire life. These symptoms are completely new to me, and they only started after my husband collapsed at the kitchen table.
Have these symptoms lasted for less than one month, or have they continued for more than one month since your husband collapsed?

They have lasted for much less than a month. It has only been about six days since my husband collapsed at our kitchen table, though it feels like a lifetime. Everything started that very same afternoon.
Since this started, do you feel emotionally numb and detached without having intrusive memories, flashbacks, or avoidance of reminders, or do you have those trauma symptoms too?

I definitely experience both. While I feel deeply numb and detached—like I'm watching someone else's life and can't feel any warmth when friends visit—I also suffer from those terrifying intrusive memories of his face turning blue. Because of that, I actively go out of my way to avoid reminders, like taking the long way around the hospital to avoid the ER.
Did you directly witness or experience the event as a life-threatening trauma, and since then have you had flashbacks, nightmares, or strong avoidance of reminders of it?

Yes, I directly witnessed my husband collapse and turn blue right in front of me, which was terrifying and felt completely life-threatening. Since then, I keep having those intrusive, flashback-like memories during the day where I see his blue face and hear him gasping, feeling like I'm right back there. I also strongly avoid reminders, forcing myself not to think about that afternoon and taking the long way around the hospital so I don't have to see the ER doors or ambulances.
Have you had any of these symptoms before this event, or is this the first time they have ever happened in your life?
No, I have never experienced anything like this before in my entire life. All of these feelings and reactions are completely new to me, and they only started after my husband collapsed six days ago.
Have these symptoms lasted for less than one month, or have they continued for more than one month since your husband collapsed?
They have lasted for much less than a month. It has only been about six days since my husband collapsed and was rushed to the hospital.
Did these symptoms begin right after the traumatic event and have they lasted less than one month, or have they continued for more than one month?

Yes, they started right away, that very afternoon my husband collapsed at the kitchen table. It has only been six days since it happened, so it is definitely much less than a month. I'm just so exhausted, even though it's only been a few days it feels like a lifetime.
Have these symptoms been present for less than one month since the event, or have they continued for more than one month?

They have been present for much less than a month, as it has only been about six days since my husband collapsed. It feels like an eternity because of how exhausted and overwhelmed I am, but it really has only been those few days.
Have these symptoms lasted for less than one month since the event, or have they continued for more than one month?
They have definitely lasted for less than a month. It has only been about six days since my husband collapsed and was rushed to the hospital.
Since this started, have you had any periods of feeling confused, unable to remember parts of what happened, or like you were in a daze and not fully aware of your surroundings?

Yes, I definitely feel like I'm in a constant daze and not fully aware of my surroundings. It's like I'm floating a few feet behind myself watching my own life like a movie, where colors and sounds feel dim and far away. I remember the event itself, but I feel completely detached and in a dreamlike state.
Before this event, have you ever had episodes like this lasting for months or starting without a clear trauma, or is this the first time and it began right after your husband's collapse?
This is the absolute first time I have ever experienced anything like this in my life. It all started exactly six days ago, right after my husband collapsed at our kitchen table.
Did these feelings of being unreal or detached start only after your husband’s collapse, or have you had similar episodes before or for months at a time?
They only started after my husband collapsed six days ago. I have never felt anything like this before in my entire life, and it is incredibly new and frightening to me.
Have you had any panic-like episodes, nightmares, or strong physical distress when reminded of the event, or is it mainly the numb, unreal feeling without those trauma symptoms?

It’s definitely not just the numb, unreal feeling. I keep having distressing memories of his face turning blue and those gurgling sounds popping into my head, and just seeing ambulances makes my stomach flip and makes me feel like I'll fall apart. I'm also incredibly jumpy now, and any sudden noise makes my heart race and sends me jumping out of my skin.
Since this started, have you also been having trouble sleeping, feeling constantly on guard, or becoming irritable or easily startled, in addition to the numb or unreal feeling?

Yes, I’ve been terribly irritable and find myself snapping at my daughter over little things like how she parks the car, which surprises me and makes me feel awful. I'm also jumping out of my skin at every sudden noise, like a monitor beeping or someone dropping a tray in the hallway, and it makes my heart race for a long time afterward.
Have these symptoms lasted for less than one month since the event, or have they continued for more than one month?
They have definitely been going on for less than a month. It has only been six days since my husband collapsed at our kitchen table, though each day feels much longer than that.
Since this started, have you had any trouble remembering important parts of what happened, or do you remember the event clearly even though it feels unreal?

No, I remember the event all too clearly. Those terrifying details—like his face turning blue and that awful gurgling sound—keep flashing back and popping into my mind vividly, even though everything around me right now feels completely unreal and dreamlike.

Since your husband’s collapse, have you had intrusive memories, flashbacks, nightmares, or strong avoidance of reminders of the event? These symptoms would point more toward PTSD than acute stress disorder.

Yes, I definitely have those. I keep seeing his face turn blue and hearing that awful gurgling sound out of nowhere, even when I'm just trying to wash the dishes. To cope, I try my best not to think about that afternoon and even walk the long way around the hospital to avoid the ER doors and ambulances, because seeing them makes me feel like I'll completely fall apart.
